questions.q: An optical fibre has core n = 1.48. (a) Calculate the critical angle [3]. (b) Explain how light travels along a curved fibre [3]. (c) Give one use [1].
questions.a: (a) sin c = 1/1.48 (1) = 0.676 (1); c = 42.5° (1); (b) light hits the core boundary at more than c (1), totally internally reflected (1), repeatedly along the fibre (1); (c) communications or endoscopes (1)

questions.q: A ray in glass (n = 1.5) hits the surface at 35°. What happens and why?
questions.a: It refracts out (with some reflection) (1) because 35° is less than the critical angle of 42° (1)

questions.q: Find n for a material whose critical angle is 30°.
State the two conditions for TIR.
questions.a: From denser to less dense medium; angle of incidence greater than the critical angle

questions.q: Why do glass prisms in binoculars work at 45°?
questions.a: 45° is greater than glass's critical angle (about 42°), so TIR occurs
